# CRA 24h Clock

> A single-file, offline command-line tool that computes the EU Cyber Resilience Act
> Article 14 reporting deadlines from your moment of awareness, drafts the ENISA/CSIRT
> notifications, and exports a CSAF 2.0 advisory. Runs entirely on your machine. No account,
> no network, no data leaves your computer. MIT licensed.

## What this answers

From **11 September 2026**, Article 14 of Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act)
obliges manufacturers of products with digital elements to report an **actively exploited
vulnerability** and **severe incidents**:

- **24 hours** — early warning to the coordinating CSIRT and ENISA
- **72 hours** — vulnerability notification with a more detailed assessment and corrective measures
- **14 days** — final report, counted from the moment a corrective measure becomes available

Two details cause most of the mistakes:

1. **The clock starts at awareness, not at confirmation.** The question an authority asks after
   an incident is "when exactly did you become aware?" — and the burden of answering it defensibly
   is on the manufacturer.
2. **The 14-day final-report clock does not start at awareness.** It starts when a corrective
   measure or mitigation becomes available. Until that exists, the deadline cannot be computed.
   This tool refuses to invent that date rather than displaying a plausible wrong one.

The obligation covers products **already on the market**, not only new releases.

## Pages

- [CRA 24h Clock — overview](https://sisuthros.github.io/cra24-clock/): what the tool does, how the deadlines are derived, and the legal basis
- [Deadline tool](https://sisuthros.github.io/cra24-clock/tool.html): enter the moment of awareness, get the 24h/72h/14d deadlines
- [Readiness assessment](https://sisuthros.github.io/cra24-clock/assess.html): questionnaire that scores whether you could actually meet a 24-hour deadline today
- [CRA in Finnish / kyberkestävyyssäädös](https://sisuthros.github.io/cra24-clock/cra-suomi.html): Finnish-language explanation, Traficom and ENISA reporting routes, authorised-representative registration
- [Incident intake](https://sisuthros.github.io/cra24-clock/intake.html): structured intake for recording an incident and its awareness timestamp

## Source and package

- Source: https://github.com/Sisuthros/cra24-clock (MIT)
- CLI entry point: `cra-clock.mjs` — requires Node.js 18+, no install step
- Deadline computation: `node cra-clock.mjs deadlines --aware 2026-09-11T08:00:00Z`
- With a known remediation date: `node cra-clock.mjs deadlines --aware <ISO> --remediation <ISO>`
- CSAF 2.0 advisory export: `csaf.mjs`
- Tests: `cra-clock.test.mjs`

## Why offline matters here

Incident timing data is among the most sensitive material a manufacturer holds: it establishes
when the company knew, which is the fact that regulatory exposure turns on. This tool performs no
network requests. Nothing is uploaded, and there is no service to trust. That is a deliberate
design constraint, and it is checkable — the tool is a single readable file.

## Known limitation

ENISA's Single Reporting Platform is a manual web form with no public API. This tool prepares the
content of the notification and the evidence of timing; the submission itself is still a human
step, and proving you submitted exactly once remains a manual problem.

## Optional

- [Guidance and hands-on setup](https://sisuthros.github.io/cra24-clock/assess.html): for teams that want the readiness assessment reviewed and the reporting process put in place rather than only the calculator
